spriteset_freedan:
Freedan player spriteset (Bank 0E, 950272-969435): every frame the player can show in form 1. 76 animations ($00-$4B), 353 frame records, 186 sprite groups, 2147 sub-sprites (at most 14 per group). Chosen by body_table[1] (art free_sprites_1AC000); SetActorBody copies the table pointer and bank into the actor ($7F0006, $7F0008). The player scripts pick the animation with StagePlayerSprite and friends; the numbering is shared with spriteset_will and spriteset_shadow.

=== FORMAT (the same in every spriteset_* file) ===

- Table: one word pointer per animation index ($28), relative to the spriteset bank.
- Frame list (sprite-set): 4-byte records < hold, &sprite_group >. A frame is shown for hold + 1 ticks. The list ends with a hidden $FFFF word that the extraction does not show (a list of n records is 4n + 2 bytes; this was checked for all 76 lists by label spacing and in the ROM). Any negative word works, AdvanceSpriteAnim tests the sign. docs/structs-reference.md says the terminator is $0000: that is wrong.
- Sprite group: 13-byte header, then 7-byte sub-sprites.
  - Header bytes 0-1: X extents (left, right); bytes 2-3: Y extents (top, bottom). UpdateActorAnimation loads them into $18/$1C and $1A/$1E (screen culling) and swaps each pair for a flipped actor.
  - Bytes 4-7: a tile-unit box read at metaspritePtr+0..3 by PlayerAttackHitTest (the attack's hit area) and by the solid-rectangle COP handlers (cop_handlers_collision): X offset and Y offset (the code ORs $FF00 into them, so they are always negative), width and height in 16-pixel units (shifted left four times). Default $F8 $F0 $01 $01 = a 16 x 16 box at (-8, -16).
  - Bytes 8-11: the body box, read at metaspritePtr+4..7 by CombatCollision (RunCombatCollision) and the interaction collision code: X offset (signed; mirrored for an H-flipped actor), width in pixels, Y offset (signed), height in pixels. Default $F8 $10 $F0 $10 = 16 x 16 at (-8, -16); some groups have other values.
  - Byte 12: the number of sub-sprites (equal to the real count in all 186 groups).
- Sub-sprite < size, x, x', y, y', tile word >: size 0 = 8x8, 1 = 16x16 (the OAM size bit); x / y is the offset inside the extent box and x' / y' the mirrored offset used for a flipped actor (x + x' = total width - size, checked by hand on three sub-sprites); the tile word is a normal OAM word (tile low byte, bit 8 name table, bits 9-11 palette, 12-13 priority, $4000 H flip, $8000 V flip).
- The same group is used by several frames and animations (353 records name 186 groups): animations $04-$07 reuse the four idle groups of $00-$03.

Tile art: the tile byte of a sub-sprite selects 32-byte tiles in free_sprites_1AC000; the player art is DMAed as the frames change (sprite_composition).

=== PLAYER ANIMATION NUMBERS ===

See the part note of the table for the index map. The previous header claimed 'Dark Friar cast poses': the ability cast in attack_ability_system stages the ordinary attack animations $36-$39, no separate Dark Friar animation was identified.
spriteset_npc_props:
Sprite set of small scene props (Bank 0E, 973312-974144, 832 bytes): the town door, a bone pile, spirits, a sign, flames, a campfire and three single-frame props. The old note ('town furniture, signs, chests, and decorative elements') was too broad: no chest uses it (chests are map tiles drawn by warps_interaction), and there is no furniture.

Structure (format in the spriteset_freedan block note): 11 animations, 20 sprite groups. 22 B pointer table + 102 B frame lists (8 one-frame lists of 6 B, 3 four-frame lists of 18 B) + 708 B groups.

| Index | Set | Frames (hold) | Users (actors selecting it) |
|-------|-----|---------------|-----------------------------|
| $00 | npc_props_00_door_open | 1 | town_door, open frame (1 sub-sprite) |
| $01 | npc_props_01_door_closed | 1 | town_door closed frame (6 sub-sprites); fr32_guide |
| $02 | npc_props_02_bones | 1 | bone pile: gs2B_bones, nvAC_bones, eu9D_bones; also btDE_olman and pyCD_jackal |
| $03 | npc_props_03 | 1 | no actor |
| $04 | npc_props_04_spirit | 4 (5 each) | spirits: awBF_spirit_guide, btDF_spirits, btE3_dao_travel_spirit, btE4_olman, daC3_babel_travel_spirit, ec10_dp_hint_spirit, mu66_rama_spirits, sE5_epilogue, btDE_olman |
| $05 | npc_props_05_sign | 1 | av69_signs |
| $06 | npc_props_06_flame | 4 (3 each) | flames: av6B_flame, ec0A_torch1, ec0A_torch2 |
| $07 | npc_props_07_street_prop | 1 | freejia_street_prop |
| $08 | npc_props_08_campfire | 4 (3 each) | st68_campfire |
| $09 | npc_props_09 | 1 | no actor |
| $0A | npc_props_0A_kara | 1 | btE4_kara |

Users were found by searching for SetMetasprite ( @spriteset_npc_props ) and reading the Stage* operand that follows it (E2); the images were not viewed, so the descriptions of $02, $05, $07 and $0A come from the actor names (OQ-I068-1). Animations $03 and $09 have no user (OQ-I068-2).
spriteset_pickups_effects:
Shared effects, pickups and props sprite set (Bank 0E, 974848-982479, 7631 bytes). The old note ('shared by all dungeon enemies, boss sub-sprites, dark gem animations and combat VFX', 'the largest spriteset file in the game') was too broad: 84 extracted actor files select it with SetMetasprite ( @spriteset_pickups_effects ), and most of them are pickups, switches, effects and scene props; only a few enemies and bosses use it (sE8_dark_gaia, ir29_castoth, sg55_viper, gw8A_sand_fanger, mu67_vampires, pyDD_mummy_queen, ec0D_canal_worm, sg4E_nitropede and others). It is not the largest: spriteset_will (17441 B), spriteset_shadow (12443 B) and spriteset_transform_poses (11653 B) are bigger.

Structure (format in the spriteset_freedan block note): 63 animations ($00-$3E), 257 frame records, 144 printed groups (one hides a second, see sprite_group_0EEE5E), 640 printed sub-sprite rows. Byte budget: 126 B pointer table + 1154 B frame lists (257 x 4 + 63 x 2) + 6351 B of groups = 7631.

Animations whose users were traced (E2):

| Index | User |
|-------|------|
| $00 | hidden_red_jewel |
| $01 | EnemyDeathFlash and the DebrisBurstParticle of SpawnDebrisBurst (eight frames, 19 ticks) |
| $04, $05, $06 | the 1, 2 and 5 gem pickups of EnemyDropSystem; $06 is also the static frame of idle_sprite_display |
| $09, $0A, $0B | the blink phase of those three pickups |
| $0C, $0D, $0E | the HP, STR and DEF stat pickups (reward_actors, field_reveal_object) |
| $0F, $10 | hit_switch (resting frame $0F, struck frame $10) |
| $22, $35 | the 5 HP heal pickup of EnemyDropSystem |
| $25, $29 | SpawnFieldRevealEffect (flash and rise) |

The other animations belong to the scene actors listed above; they were not mapped one by one (OQ-I069-2).
